name: Sinking Ships
label: Revelation
lede: A Seattle band that hid ten copies of its first record around the city like Easter eggs, made one album for Revelation, and was done inside five years.

eras.title: A treasure hunt in Seattle
eras.text: Sinking Ships came out of Seattle's hardcore scene in 2004, fronted by Danny Hesketh, whose brother Jim sang in Champion. Their records were as much objects as music: hand-numbered, vellum-wrapped, hidden in the city.

years.p: Danny Hesketh sings, Paul Betinson plays guitar and Colin Horn plays bass. Punknews would later note Hesketh's brother Jim fronted the Seattle band Champion.

years.h: Sinking Ships hide ten records around Seattle
years.p: The demo comes out as a 7" on Excursion Records: 500 hand-numbered clear copies with vellum covers, and ten speckled copies hidden around Seattle as a Treasure Hunt Press.
Five songs recorded at the Autopsy Room with Jesse O'Donnell, including 39th and Glisan. Run For Cover repressed it in 2006 as RFC 003.

eras.title: The Revelation years
eras.text: Revelation signed them for a debut album that Punknews called one of the best hardcore records going. For two more years they toured hard and pressed their own singles in batches of 500.

years.p: Twelve songs in about 29 minutes, recorded by Jesse O'Donnell. Scott Freeman of [[Shook Ones|de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f]] guests on The Next Time I Go.
years.xp: Punknews heard latter-era [[Turning Point|19b7cbc9-0898-400a-87d5-bfa47c87487c]] in it and joked the guitar tone needed a chiropractor. The review praised the band for skipping posi slogans and straight edge posturing in favor of darker songs about desperation and small towns.

years.p: Four songs, including Irish Wristwatch and Wallingford Is Still Doomed, named for the Seattle neighborhood.

years.h: Spray-painted singles for the European tour
years.p: Safe / Revenge, recorded at Sound West in Tacoma, is the first release on the band's own Sinking Ships Records: 500 copies, a handful in badly spray-painted covers sold on their European tour.

years.h: Out of Touch / Bee Honda: blue for Sound and Fury, gold by mail
years.p: The second Sinking Ships Records single: 250 blue copies sold at the Sound and Fury festival, 250 gold by mail order only.

years.h: Sinking Ships play Rainfest and tour with Comeback Kid
years.p: Sinking Ships play Rainfest in 2008 and share bills with [[Comeback Kid|6d152109-c447-446d-9a06-3621c920bebd]], [[Down to Nothing|fac027c9-e8db-4546-9515-9d48d1a7185c]], [[Shook Ones|de5db393-7bcd-4ddc-98c7-1e9a48366f3f]] and [[Blacklisted|00330ad2-6d94-4957-b3b0-7ca1ea6f6fd6]]. There's also a Japan-only split with As We Let Go and My Love on Alliance Trax.
Four years in, with one album and a stack of 7"s, Sinking Ships break up at the end of 2008.

eras.title: One more time
eras.text: Five years after the split, the core of the band came back briefly, and Disconnecting got a remastered reissue.

years.h: Sinking Ships reunite, and Disconnecting is remastered
years.p: Danny Hesketh, Paul Betinson and Colin Horn bring Sinking Ships back for a brief 2013 reunion, alongside a remastered reissue of Disconnecting.
